reason: The cited evidence confirms that SRO can be induced by heat treatment and measured by APT in CrCoNi (E1), and that the as-rolled alloy has low yield strength (~350 MPa) needing improvement (E2). However, the specific mechanistic claims that SRO simultaneously enhances strength, modulus, ductility, and fracture resistance are not supported by the cited passages, which do not report mechanical property outcomes from SRO-inducing annealing.
premises: Annealing after hot-rolling can induce atomic short-range order (SRO) in CrCoNi-based alloys.
SRO can be quantified experimentally, e.g., by atom probe tomography (APT).
SRO increases local bond strength and creates structural heterogeneity.
SRO impedes dislocation motion, increasing strength and Young's modulus.
SRO facilitates intrinsic toughening, improving ductility and fracture resistance.
